label: <DEL> step when the first token to copy is in {p,l,x,o,1,z,i,n,r,f,s,3}; also input e in the original phase
explanation: Two modes. (1) The delimiter step, which carries 57% of activation mass and all of the strongest activations. It fires on 31% of <DEL> steps, and whether it does depends mostly on the first original token, which is the token about to be output. Rates are highest for p, l and x (23-29%), then o, 1, z, i, n, r, f, s and 3. Rates are also higher for short sequences (13% of steps at L=3). The top activations are all at <DEL> after sequences starting with x or l. (2) The input e during the original phase, active on about 61% of those steps and carrying about 29% of mass. Precision rises to 75% when two or more tokens are still to come. It is weak in the copy phase (2.8% rate, 12% mass) and rarely fires on other original-phase inputs. Restricting the delimiter mode to the first-token set gives about 65% precision but drops some delimiter activations, so the predicate is incomplete. Dev split: F1 0.62, mass recall 0.80.
